title: WoW's Most Famous Video, Leeroy Jenkins, Was Staged
hook: On May 11, 2005 a guild called Pals for Life uploaded a WoW raid clip where Leeroy Jenkins charged in alone and wiped everyone, and years later its makers said it was staged. Blizzard still gave him an achievement and a Hearthstone card. Would you have followed him in?
script: Did you know the most famous World of Warcraft video ever made was staged? On May eleventh, two thousand five, a guild called Pals for Life uploaded a raid clip to WarcraftMovies. In it, the raid spends minutes carefully planning a pull in the Rookery of Upper Blackrock Spire. One player works out a thirty two percent chance of survival. Then a paladin named Leeroy Jenkins comes back from making chicken, yells his own name, and charges in alone. The whole raid follows him and everybody dies. Leeroy was played by a guy named Ben Schulz, and the clip spread across the internet within weeks. For years fans argued about whether it was real. More than a decade later, the makers said it was a setup, a parody of guilds that took raiding too seriously. Blizzard embraced it anyway. The game got an achievement called Leeroy, spelled with a long row of extra letters, earned in that same Rookery. And Leeroy became a Hearthstone card that is still famous for how aggressive it is. That scripted disaster is still part of the game two decades later. Would you have followed Leeroy in? Follow for more gaming history.
